task.description:
Test design gate for REQ-069 (WF-02 step 5b). This is the FIRST pass of this gate for this run (maximum three passes: first and two repeats). You work in a copy; you change only your handoff. No commits, no git checkout/reset/stash/clean (also not in scratch copies). 16 GB RAM computer: single commands, one test run at a time, close everything you started.

Read: the design docs/design/REQ-069-tenant-look-format.md (criterion-to-test table, was-to-became table A1-A7/B1-B8, the mutant list MU01-MU70, quality bar section), docs/requirements.yaml REQ-069 and the micro-amendment MA069, decisions 0084 and 0085, the result of step 12 (self_check table of mutants), and the new and changed tests: tools/test/picker-look.test.js, picker-look-property.test.js, picker-look-helpers.js, the sample folder tools/test/fixtures/picker-look/ (89 files), SV-9a..SV-9f in picker-server.test.js, and the changed old tests (diff against the tag base/LOOK069-20261026-01).

Check yourself, do not trust the report:
(1) Every criterion of REQ-069 (and MA069) has a runnable test that fails when the criterion is broken; list criterion to test; nothing is skipped, todo or conditional.
(2) Oracles are independent of the code: the helper has its own contrast function, own sign class, own catalogues and literal message texts M01-M37; no test imports the checked functions to compute its own expected value (imports used only to call them). Samples are literal expected lines, not computed by the code.
(3) The old guard tests repaired by the was-to-became table: each repaired test keeps its ban (no assertion weakened, no count lowered without the table saying so); the seven expected red ones are now green for the stated reasons only. Compare the diff yourself.
(4) The tests are independent of each other and of order and clock (run the picker test files twice, once in reverse file order if the runner allows; the property test uses a pinned seed; no network, no fixed port, no leftover temp folders).
(5) Mutants: apply yourself, one at a time on a scratch copy of tools/ (restore the file from the live tree after each run), at least these: all of the design list MU01-MU70 that are NOT trivially of one kind (take every fifth mutant of the design list plus all of MU02, MU03, MU20, MU35, MU44, MU55, MU56, MU62, MU65) and at least FIVE mutants of your own that are not in the list (for example: the contrast check using a wrong threshold for only one of the object roles, the order of two checks swapped, the staff-name class accepting an empty value after trimming, a chips duplicate check comparing only neighbours at even places, the /3 mode accepted for a different case of the schema string). Every mutant must make at least one test red; report equivalent mutants separately with a reason. Also check that the six /1 and /2 demo answers sha256 literals in SV-9c equal the output of the tag version (run the server on a clean copy of the tag).
(6) The quality bar items named in REQ-069 each have a test or a stated check.
(7) Run `npm run check` once in the live tree at the end: it must be green (2043 tests expected) and the sha256 of tools/src must not change.
Verdict PASS or FAIL. Findings with severity, file, line and the fix wanted; Low findings go to the follow-up list. In your handoff text never list project names or machine paths (say "the traces list").
